messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — follow up + dataset/requested goals

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to see the reranking flow and the examples you shared. To recap the key items we agreed on and the next steps from Redwood: 

- Goal: improve search/recommendation ranking quality for product search with emphasis on NDCG@10 uplift and MRR for head+long tail. You mentioned current baseline NDCG@10 ~0.42 and MRR ~0.31 across samples.
- Constraints: strict latency SLO (~120ms p50 rerank stage), cost target ~<$0.02/query in production, and no PII allowed in training/eval sets.
- Data: you agreed to share a representative eval set and the current labeling schema (clicks / purchases / human labels).
- Next steps (from Redwood): we will run an initial model-fit evaluation across 3 candidate rerankers, produce an NDCG/MRR summary, and propose an A/B test plan with sample size estimates. We'll also surface any quality regressions vs your current baseline.

Can you please: 
1) Share the evaluation CSV (query_id, doc_id, relevance, click_weight, rank) and a short sample of 500 rows for quick sanity checks.
2) Confirm whether we can run an offline A/B simulation using historical logs (you said yes on the call).
3) Tell us who should be looped into procurement for the Dedicated environment (if we need a sandbox GPU vs hosted).

I attached a short template for the eval CSV and a sample prompt set we typically use for rerank candidate scoring.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

P.S. We'll aim to have an initial evaluation summary by EOD Wed (Pacific).

Hi Samir/Lara —

Attached is our initial evaluation plan and the prompt-set-sample.jsonl we referenced on the call. Summary of our proposed approach: 

1) Candidates to test (offline):
  - redwood-rerank-1.0 (cross-encoder style, 3B dense, recommended primary)
  - cross-encoder-3b-quant (int8 quantized build for cost experiments)
  - lightweight-bi-ensemble (small bi-encoder + learned combiner for latency-sensitive pathways)

2) Metrics we will report: NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, mean latency (p50/p95), token cost per query, and regression rate on your 1k guardrail set.

3) Benchmarks & links: we pushed a preliminary summary to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-rerank-evals and a HubSpot record for visibility: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/ACME-2026-087.

4) A/B plan (high level):
  - Offline simulation first to validate expected uplift and identify regressions.
  - If offline looks good, run a 2-week A/B with 10% traffic vs control; we'll propose exact sample sizes after the offline pass.

5) Security/compliance: we will not persist any raw PII and will run evals inside your scrubbed logs; our Private deployment option is available if you prefer we don't process in hosted.

Attachments: ndcg-mrr-summary.pdf (initial placeholder), prompt-set-sample.jsonl, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Would you like us to prioritize cost-optimized configs (quantized) or start with highest-quality and then iterate?

Thanks,
Marissa

marissa@redwood.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recommended models + initial eval plan (includes benchmarks & prompt set)

Samir / Marissa —

Quick technical notes from the evaluation team after running the 500-row sample Samir sent: 

- Sanity: data format looks good and labels align with our expectations. Minor issue: a small fraction (0.6%) of rows have empty relevance; we'll ignore those for aggregated metrics.

- Initial offline results (500-sample quick pass):
  - Current baseline (Acme prod ranker): NDCG@10 = 0.418, MRR = 0.312
  - redwood-rerank-1.0: NDCG@10 = 0.496 (+0.078), MRR = 0.365 (+0.053)
  - cross-encoder-3b-quant: NDCG@10 = 0.478 (+0.060), MRR = 0.349 (+0.037)
  - lightweight-bi-ensemble: NDCG@10 = 0.452 (+0.034), MRR = 0.331 (+0.019)

- Latency (rerank-only, median measured on test harness):
  - redwood-rerank-1.0: p50 = 95ms, p95 = 220ms
  - cross-encoder-3b-quant: p50 = 68ms, p95 = 140ms
  - lightweight-bi-ensemble: p50 = 28ms, p95 = 80ms

- Regression guardrail check on the 1k hand-curated queries: redwood-rerank-1.0 had 1.2% regressions (items with lower relevance than baseline). We recommend adding a small rerank threshold / constraint to reduce user-visible regressions during rollout.

- A/B sample size: to detect the observed NDCG uplift (~0.078) at 90% power with two-sided test, we estimate roughly 120k queries per variant (this will be refined on full eval set). For a 2-week run at 10% traffic, this is feasible for Acme's traffic profile per Samir's note.

I'll attach the detailed CSV and the script we used for metrics. Next steps: run full offline evaluation on the full eval CSV (we'll queue this overnight) and then provide a finalized A/B plan with exact sample sizes and monitoring criteria (regression thresholds, user-impact metrics).

\u0014 Dylan Brooks
Principal ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai
